narrative: Material PL1__M0E3F279 exhibits regular, gamma-like demand (CV=0.62, mean=385 units/day) with no discernible trend over the observed horizon. Lead times are highly variable (CV=1.27, mean=0.85 days), necessitating a robust safety stock of 777 units. The (r,Q) policy with reorder point 1,523 and order quantity 6,590 units consolidates orders from ~127 to ~15 per year, cutting total annual cost by 80.7%. Storage capacity is fully utilised and should be reviewed if demand grows.
warnings: HIGH - CAPACITY_CONSTRAINT: Storage capacity limits order quantity to 6590 units (EOQ suggests 8785)
MEDIUM - HIGH_LEAD_TIME_VARIABILITY: Lead time CV of 1.27 indicates unstable supply; consider supplier performance review
MEDIUM - HIGH_DEMAND_VARIABILITY: Demand CV of 0.62 suggests high variability; review demand planning accuracy
MEDIUM - HIGH_CAPACITY_UTILIZATION: Capacity utilization at ~100% leaves minimal buffer for demand spikes

research_insights.selection_rationale: Regular demand (91.9% non-zero days) with gamma-like variability and a well-defined mean makes a continuous-review (r,Q) policy appropriate. The EOQ minimises ordering+holding costs, and the reorder point incorporates stochastic lead-time demand variability to meet the 95% service level target.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is binding: the EOQ of 8,785 exceeds available space, capping the order quantity at 6,590. This increases ordering frequency slightly above the unconstrained optimum and leaves no buffer room post-replenishment. If demand spikes immediately after a delivery, a stockout risk above the modelled 5% tail exists until the next order.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility (MOQ 757 + SS 777 = 1,534 < 7,368 max). Capacity constraint is binding but resolvable within current MOQ parameters. Recommend warehouse capacity review to allow full EOQ deployment.
